title: Automated audit briefs and regional residency ledgers
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver a new reporting capability that produces compact, verifiable audit briefs (1-page PDF) and full evidence ledgers (CSV + signed manifest) scoped to tenant residency. Exports must be region-aware, include retention metadata, and support multiple delivery targets (S3 presigned, secure SFTP, SIEM webhook). The feature should be schedulable and usable from the Console and API, and include observable traces for delivery success/failure and retention enforcement.
background: Customers in regulated industries ask for regularly-scheduled compliance artifacts that prove where data was stored and why it was retained or deleted. Existing export features generate large archives but lack concise audit summaries, cryptographic manifests, region-aware snapshots, and flexible delivery channels. This initiative complements ongoing work on tenant-scoped retention settings and the scheduled exports backlog (see PM-4128) by adding a signed ledger and short audit brief for reviewers and auditors.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console and API allow creating a scheduled export job that produces: a 1-page PDF audit brief, a CSV evidence ledger, and a signed manifest (SHA256) for each run
2) Every export honors tenant data residency settings: artifacts for EU-resident tenants are produced and stored in EU regions only unless explicit override is set
3) Manifest includes per-file checksum, export start/end timestamps, retention policy id, KMS key id used to sign the manifest, and export job id

4) Delivery supports at least three targets: S3 with presigned URL and region-scoped bucket, secure SFTP endpoint, and a configurable SIEM/webhook; failures are retried with exponential backoff and recorded in export history
5) Scheduled runs surface compact telemetry in Console: last run status, items exported, size, time-to-generate, and a link to the artifact location; raw logs are citable from the job page

6) Retention enforcement: exported artifacts include retention metadata and a linked retention policy; downstream auto-delete jobs can purge artifacts according to tenant policy and produce a post-deletion manifest
7) Security review completed; KMS signing pattern and tenant key access validated; export pipeline passes threat model checklist
8) Automated tests cover scheduling, residency routing, manifest generation, and delivery failure/retry paths

notes: Design to include both human-readable audit brief and machine-readable ledger to satisfy auditors and automated tooling
Consider adding a lightweight signed token in the brief that verifies the manifest without downloading large archives
Retention metadata must be persisted in the export manifest to prove deletion timelines
Explore optional encryption-at-rest with tenant-managed keys for artifact buckets in later phase
